source.research_status: current reports of the research team

status_meaning.pass: a registered finite test of the row passed on the OPH law

rows.name: Charge quantization
rows.test: integer topological charge; a split e → e/2 + e/2 impossible
rows.explain: Electric charge comes in whole units. OpenWave asks for a charge that is an integer topological number, a winding that cannot be split, so that e → e/2 + e/2 is impossible.

rows.name: Electron rest energy (mass)
rows.test: a localized state the dynamics selects, set to 511 keV by one anchor; validated when a second quantity fixed by that anchor agrees with measurement
rows.explain: A particle at rest carries energy E = mc². OpenWave asks for a localized state that the dynamics itself selects, set to 511 keV by one anchor, and a second quantity fixed by that anchor that agrees with measurement.

rows.name: de Broglie clock (Zitterbewegung)
rows.test: self-starting frequency-rigid internal oscillation at ω = mc²/ℏ
rows.explain: Quantum theory gives every massive particle an internal oscillation at ω = mc²/ℏ, a clock it carries along. OpenWave asks for a self-starting internal oscillation whose frequency is rigid.

rows.name: Particle stability (Derrick escape)
rows.test: the particle state persists in free evolution
rows.explain: A particle has to hold together on its own. OpenWave asks for a localized state that persists in free evolution, with no trap, against the Derrick-type escape by which classical field lumps spread or collapse.
rows.result: A signed circulation of a bound pair around one plaquette is an eigenvector of every update of the OPH law, at every age of the pair, with eigenvalue −exp(iφ/2): its profile never changes, and its overlap with the state a capture writes is zero at every address, so a returning marker cannot release it. The observers recorded zero separations in five cohorts of 4,194,304 trials. Giving the two constituents independent transport separated 3,144,922 of 4,194,304 pairs, where the law gives exactly three quarters. An ordinary collision does not populate this mode: its first closed return separates 0.47253% of the marked pairs.

rows.name: Magnetic moment μ (g ≈ 2, magnetostatics)
rows.test: intrinsic magnetostatics: a stationary state sources a static dipole B from internal circulation, g ≈ 2; dipole Larmor response
rows.explain: A spinning charge acts as a small magnet. OpenWave asks for intrinsic magnetostatics: a stationary state whose internal circulation sources a static dipole field B, with g ≈ 2 and the Larmor response to an applied field.

rows.name: Angular momentum J (spin ℏ/2)
rows.test: field-carried J = ℏ/2 on the electron state
rows.explain: The electron carries angular momentum ℏ/2. OpenWave asks for that angular momentum carried by the field of the electron state itself.

rows.name: Spin-½ statistics (720° double cover)
rows.test: a measured sign of −1 under a 2π rotation or under the exchange of two cores; a half turn that the dynamics selects against a polar control earns partial
rows.explain: A spin-½ object returns to itself only after two full turns: one turn of 360° multiplies its state by −1. OpenWave asks for a measured sign of −1 under a 2π rotation or the exchange of two cores.

rows.name: Antimatter + annihilation
rows.test: pair annihilation to radiation; follow-on: positronium 2γ/3γ
rows.explain: Every particle has an antiparticle, and a pair can annihilate into radiation. OpenWave asks for pair annihilation into radiation, with positronium decaying into two or three photons as a follow-on.

rows.name: Neutrinos (neutral states)
rows.test: light charge-0 states released in decays
rows.explain: Some particles carry no charge and barely interact. OpenWave asks for light, charge-zero states released in decays.

rows.name: Neutrino oscillations (PMNS)
rows.test: 3 flavors + oscillation; the PMNS angles
rows.explain: Neutrinos change flavour as they travel. OpenWave asks for three flavours that oscillate, with the angles of the PMNS matrix.

rows.name: Lepton mass spectrum (μ, τ)
rows.test: exactly 3 charged-lepton minima; ratios 1 : 207 : 3477
rows.explain: The electron has two heavier copies, the muon and the tau. OpenWave asks for exactly three charged-lepton minima with mass ratios 1 : 207 : 3477.

rows.name: Quarks
rows.test: fractional charge as partial winding on a quark string
rows.explain: Quarks carry a third or two thirds of the electron's charge and come in three colours. OpenWave asks for fractional charge as a partial winding on a quark string.

rows.name: Baryons: bound state (p, n)
rows.test: a stable three-quark composite
rows.explain: Three quarks bind into a proton or neutron. OpenWave asks for a stable three-quark composite.

rows.name: Baryons: mass ordering + charge profile
rows.test: m_n > m_p; positive core, negative shell
rows.explain: The neutron is slightly heavier than the proton, and the proton has a positive core and a negative shell. OpenWave asks for that mass ordering and charge profile.

rows.name: Baryons: exact masses
rows.test: 938.3 / 939.6 MeV from the field
rows.explain: The proton and neutron weigh 938.3 and 939.6 MeV. OpenWave asks for those masses from the field.

rows.name: Deuteron (binding + quadrupole)
rows.test: m_d < m_p + m_n; the electric quadrupole moment
rows.explain: A proton and a neutron bind into the deuteron, lighter than its parts and slightly elongated. OpenWave asks for m_d < m_p + m_n and the electric quadrupole.

rows.name: Nuclear structure (levels, halos)
rows.test: binding curve, levels, halo-nuclei lifetimes
rows.explain: Nuclei show a binding-energy curve, discrete levels and loosely bound halo nuclei. OpenWave asks for the binding curve, levels and halo lifetimes.

rows.name: Mesons (π, K)
rows.test: π/K states; strange decays (Λ⁰ → p + π⁻)
rows.explain: Mesons are quark-antiquark pairs such as the pion and the kaon. OpenWave asks for π and K states and strange decays such as Λ⁰ → p + π⁻.

rows.name: Dark matter candidate
rows.test: a stable neutral massive state
rows.explain: Most matter in the Universe is dark: neutral, massive and stable. OpenWave asks for a stable neutral massive state.

rows.name: Electric force (Coulomb 1/r, electrostatics)
rows.test: far-field 1/r potential at charge e; the strength (α) credited only when it follows from the model's own mechanism, never fitted
rows.explain: Two charges feel a force whose potential falls off as 1/r. OpenWave asks for that far-field potential at charge e, with the strength α credited only when the model's own mechanism produces it.

rows.name: Lorentz covariance (+ Coulomb = EM)
rows.test: Lorentz-invariant action, no preferred frame; boosted states contract, c-limited
rows.explain: The laws of physics look the same to every observer moving at constant speed: moving clocks slow, moving rods shorten, and nothing outruns light. OpenWave asks for a Lorentz-invariant action with no preferred frame, contracted boosted states and a limiting speed c.

rows.name: Strong force: confinement
rows.test: linear inter-charge potential, ~1 GeV/fm (Cornell)
rows.explain: Quarks never appear alone: the energy between them grows linearly with distance, about 1 GeV per femtometre. OpenWave asks for that linear inter-charge potential.

rows.name: Running coupling
rows.test: coupling varies with scale (onset at the core radius)
rows.explain: The strength of a force changes with the scale at which it is probed. OpenWave asks for a coupling that varies with scale, with its onset at the core radius.

rows.name: Weak force: muon decay
rows.test: μ relaxes to e + neutral ejecta
rows.explain: The muon decays into an electron and two neutrinos. OpenWave asks for a muon that relaxes into an electron plus neutral ejecta.

rows.name: Weak force: beta decay (n → p)
rows.test: n → p + e + ν̄, parity-violating (needs a neutron)
rows.explain: A neutron decays into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino, and the weak force prefers one handedness. OpenWave asks for n → p + e + ν̄ with parity violation.

rows.name: Gravity: Newton limit (GEM)
rows.test: attractive 1/r² between masses, via the GEM route; the strength (G) credited only when it follows from the model's own mechanism, never fitted
rows.explain: Masses attract with a force that falls off as 1/r². OpenWave asks for that attraction through the gravito-electromagnetic route, with G credited only when the model's own mechanism produces it.

rows.name: Gravity: local metric phenomena
rows.test: light bending, gravitational time dilation / Shapiro delay
rows.explain: Mass bends light and slows clocks. OpenWave asks for light bending, gravitational time dilation and the Shapiro delay.

rows.name: Cosmology: Λ / cosmic acceleration
rows.test: Λ from the model's own mechanism, never fitted; every remaining gap and a falsification named
rows.explain: The expansion of the Universe accelerates, driven by a cosmological constant Λ. OpenWave asks for Λ from the model's own mechanism, with every gap and a falsification named.

rows.name: EM waves (Maxwell)
rows.test: Maxwell recovered; transverse waves at c
rows.explain: Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave travelling at c. OpenWave asks for Maxwell's equations recovered, with transverse waves at c.

rows.name: Quantum wave equation (Klein-Gordon)
rows.test: emergent ω² = k² + m² for matter waves
rows.explain: Matter is a wave: a free particle with mass m and wave number k oscillates at ω with ω² = k² + m². OpenWave asks for that relation to emerge for matter waves.
rows.result: Matter launched from an ordinary encounter meets the emergent massive dispersion test: all 72 held comparisons on prepared waves and all 40 nonzero forecasts from a separate point launch passed, with no material mass fitted. The observers forecast the frequencies from phase translations and an independently calibrated signal speed, and halving the private circumference nearly doubles each of the first three rest gaps. On the compact collision branch fourteen signed axial and oblique directions passed both bounds at each of periods 64, 128 and 256. Refining the public and private phase increments together yields the Klein–Gordon equation with the calibrated limiting speed.

rows.name: Orbital quantization (atomic structure)
rows.test: hydrogen-like discrete levels from standing waves
rows.explain: Atoms have discrete energy levels because bound electron waves must fit as standing waves. OpenWave asks for hydrogen-like discrete levels from standing waves.
